teams.heading: Jake White reported as leading candidate for Fiji head coach job
teams.body: The Fiji head coach search has a leading name. Jake White, the former Springboks coach, was reported last week as the frontrunner for the job. A fresh search also turned up a report describing a World Cup-winning coach as the favourite for the post ahead of the 2027 World Cup. The search began when Fiji Rugby and Mick Byrne parted ways by mutual agreement in April, 18 months before the tournament.

lead.why: It is the only Fiji story in today's pack with a fresh search hit, and it is a live selection question for the national team.

teams.heading: England's Tom Curry out of Sale side with illness before Harlequins clash
teams.body: Tom Curry has withdrawn from Sale Sharks' side with illness, forcing director of rugby Alex Sanderson into a reshuffle for Sale's round three PREM clash with Harlequins. The England back-rower was due to start on the openside against the bottom-ranked Londoners. Christ Tshiunza now comes into the back row, while Sam Dugdale is promoted onto the bench.

lead.why: A fresh England-linked late change, not one of the stories already run this week.

teams.heading: France's next Nations Championship Test is Fiji in Round four
teams.body: France's next Test is against Fiji in Round four of the Nations Championship. The fixture follows a 42-15 win over Japan in Round three, which took France to two wins from three matches, with their only defeat coming in that run. Across those three games they have scored 116 points and conceded 75, a points difference of +41.

teams.heading: Munster name Avan Lee interim chief executive as Ian Flanagan steps down
teams.body: Munster have appointed New Zealander Avan Lee as interim chief executive, with Ian Flanagan stepping down after months of heavy criticism over governance. Lee is a former Hurricanes chief, described in coverage as an experienced Super Rugby franchise boss. The moves were reported earlier this month, and the interim appointment leaves the permanent chief executive role unfilled.

teams.heading: Italy's 34-19 win over Chile is their biggest win in last 11
teams.body: Across their last 11 games, Italy have scored 190 points and conceded 318, which works out at averages of 17.3 scored and 28.9 conceded a game. Their biggest win in that window was a 34-19 home victory over Chile in November 2025, an International Friendlies fixture. Gonzalo Quesada's side face the reigning world champions, South Africa, in round four of the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Darcy Graham ruled out of Scotland's autumn Tests with ruptured bicep
teams.body: Darcy Graham is out of Scotland's autumn Tests with a ruptured bicep, according to reports on 25 September that ruled the winger out of the November window. A search headline since then describes him as out for the rest of the year, but today's search found no newer update on his recovery or any return date. Scotland's next fixture is against New Zealand, and Graham's absence is an autumn injury blow the squad must plan around.

teams.heading: Tom Rogers wins man of the match at 15 in Ospreys win
teams.body: Tom Rogers was named man of the match as Ospreys beat Dragons at Rodney Parade, taking over the 15 jersey after starting on the wing. Ospreys head coach Mark Jones said: "I really loved the way he beat the first man almost every time to get us on the front foot." Rogers scored a Wales hat-trick against New Zealand in November 2025, and Steve Tandy has plenty to ponder before naming his Nations Championship squad.

lead.why: A new Wales selection story, with Tom Rogers' full-back-or-wing audition and Steve Tandy's squad decision still to come.

teams.heading: Two men jailed for murder of former Argentina rugby player Aramburú
teams.body: Weeks ago, two men were given lengthy jail terms for the murder of Aramburú, a former Argentina rugby player. It is far from the pitch, but it concerns one of the Pumas' own. On the field, Argentina's next opponent is Ireland in the Nations Championship, and Los Pumas come in having lost 24-31 to England in Round 3 after one win from three.

teams.heading: Les Kiss vows Wallabies will return fire in Sydney Bledisloe rematch
teams.body: Les Kiss has already turned to next Saturday's Bledisloe Cup rematch at Accor Stadium in Sydney, insisting the Wallabies will go back to work and return fire after the 50-19 loss at Eden Park. It was the first defeat of Kiss's tenure, ending a five-match unbeaten run, and he said the review would focus on how to get Australia's strengths into the game while nullifying New Zealand's. New Zealand have now retained the Bledisloe Cup for a 23rd successive year.

lead.why: Kiss's response to the Eden Park loss sets up the Sydney rematch, the most forward-looking Wallabies angle in today's coverage.

teams.heading: Hajime Shoji admits League One lacked communication before eligibility U-turn
teams.body: In late August, Japan Rugby League One backtracked on player registration rules that would have classed some Japanese passport-holders born abroad as foreigners, limiting their domestic opportunities. After legal challenges and a fierce backlash from players, the league's exception now covers those who acquired Japanese citizenship by May 2025. Managing Executive Director Hajime Shoji admitted the league had lacked communication with affected players. The rules were due to take effect in the 2026-27 season, which begins in December.

lead.why: The eligibility rollback is the only shortlist item with a Japan-side stake that hasn't already run in this tab, and it has the most detail to work with.

teams.heading: Rennie says Jordie Barrett has 'taken his game to another level'
teams.body: Jordie Barrett has been the standout of the first Bledisloe Cup Test, and Dave Rennie says the inside centre has "taken his game to another level" after New Zealand's 50-19 win over Australia at Eden Park. Rennie praised Barrett's defence and physicality, while captain Codie Taylor said the 29-year-old acts almost as an extra forward. Barrett's influence at 12 also helped Damian McKenzie produce a stellar showing at fly-half, with Richie Mo'unga and Ruben Love both out injured.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the shortlist, and it gives a fan a fresh talking point about Barrett's form and his role at 12.

teams.heading: URC: Springbok Bongi Mbonambi faces Sharks disciplinary hearing over camp conduct
teams.body: Springbok hooker Bongi Mbonambi is at the centre of a URC disciplinary matter at the Sharks, according to Rapport, which reports he did not abide by JP Pietersen's rules during the squad's pre-season team-building camp. Mbonambi, a 2019 and 2023 World Cup winner, has been out of action for the Sharks in the first three rounds, and the presiding officer is expected to rule within two weeks. Fez Mbatha and Eduan Swart reportedly received warning letters.

lead.why: A new, South Africa-relevant discipline story about a Springbok hooker that no earlier edition has covered.
